title: Image requests stopped waiting on the wrong things
summary:
Image generation got tighter limits and fewer unnecessary waits, while model listings became a better reflection of what the services actually offer.

Image responses no longer wait for telemetry, and cache hits skip an unnecessary provider lookup. The generated-image cache was ultimately capped at 1,000 entries, evicting the oldest when full, while progress bars stopped filling non-TTY logs. Less waiting, less unbounded growth.

Azure Flux Kontext prompt and input-image safety checks now time out after 30 seconds. A stalled check returns a timeout error instead of holding a queue slot indefinitely. An interim tighter anonymous queue limit was also reverted; anonymous and registered requests can each use up to five slots.

Enter’s OpenAI-compatible model-list proxy now requests the upstream model-list path rather than its root, so it returns models instead of a redirect. Unused services and orphaned model IDs were removed, leaving the shared registry aligned with 18 available services. The image registry now lists flux, kontext, turbo, and gptimage, with corrected provider metadata for the first three.

Green Hope AI joined the creative projects list with AI thumbnail generation and editable text, placement, styles, and effects. A separate Next.js email utility was also added, with reusable templates and endpoints for custom and welcome emails; it is not connected to existing Pollinations services.
